chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Hudhayl ibn Hanan, brother of Ja'far ibn Hanan, said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I have entrusted to my brother Ja'far ibn Hanan some wealth that was mine, and he gives me what I spend, and I perform Hajj from it and give charity. I have asked those among us, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not permissible. I wish to conclude regarding this matter with your opinion, so what do you say?
He said: Did he give you [what you spent] before you entrusted your wealth to him?
He said: Take from him what he gives you, eat from it, drink, perform Hajj, and give charity. So when you arrive in Iraq, say: Ja'far ibn Muhammad gave the fatwa regarding this.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to entrust wealth to a family member who pays for your living expenses and Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of validating transactions based on established custom (*urf*) and prior practice rather than rigid formalism. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the permissibility of this financial arrangement, emphasizing that continuity of benefit validates the transfer, a ruling later cited by scholars to support flexible commercial contracts. The instruction to convey the source of the ruling underscores the authority of the Imam's direct testimony in resolving local scholarly disputes.
